accepted.s: Hyderabad State was classified as a Part B State during which of the following periods?
accepted.x: Hyderabad State was a Part B State from 1950 until 31 October 1956, immediately before the formation of Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Use the exact constitutional period and distinguish the final date from the appointed day.
accepted.sec: Hyderabad State - period, Burgula ministry, merger debate, 1954 shift

accepted.s: Who headed the first elected ministry of Hyderabad State that took office in 1952?
accepted.x: Burgula Ramakrishna Rao headed the first elected ministry of Hyderabad State, which assumed office in 1952.
accepted.tq: Apply the wrong-person-with-the-deed trap by separating Hyderabad leaders from Andhra leaders.
accepted.sec: Hyderabad State - period, Burgula ministry, merger debate, 1954 shift

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Hyderabad Congress:
1. In June 1953, it resolved to divide Hyderabad State into Visalandhra, United Maharashtra and United Karnataka.
2. In 1954, the earlier three-way division resolution was set aside.
3. The 1954 position supported the separation of Hyderabad State into regions corresponding to their linguistic states.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The Hyderabad Congress first adopted the three-way division proposal in June 1953, set it aside in 1954, and then supported linguistic reorganisation of its regions.
accepted.tq: Track the change in an organisation’s position chronologically rather than treating all resolutions as one.
accepted.sec: Hyderabad State - period, Burgula ministry, merger debate, 1954 shift

accepted.s: B. Ramakrishna Rao initially supported a separate Telangana but changed his stand in 1954 and subsequently advocated which of the following?
o: The continuation of Hyderabad as a bilingual State
The merger of Telangana with United Maharashtra
The immediate merger of Telangana with Andhra
The creation of a separate Kannada-speaking State
accepted.x: B. Ramakrishna Rao changed his position in 1954 and advocated the early merger of Telangana with Andhra; he later kept Delhi informed in favour of Visalandhra.
accepted.tq: Test the before-and-after position of the same leader instead of confusing his initial stand with his later one.
accepted.sec: Hyderabad State - period, Burgula ministry, merger debate, 1954 shift

accepted.s: At the Warangal Congress meeting held on 8 July 1954, B. Ramakrishna Rao stated that, before the States Reorganisation Commission report, the Hyderabad Government had:
o: Accepted the three-way division of Hyderabad State
No official opinion, while ministers expressed personal views
Officially rejected the merger with Andhra
accepted.x: At Warangal on 8 July 1954, he stated that the Hyderabad Government had no official opinion before the SRC report and that ministers had expressed only personal views.
accepted.tq: Use the precise date and distinguish an official government position from individual ministerial opinions.
accepted.sec: Hyderabad State - period, Burgula ministry, merger debate, 1954 shift

accepted.s:
Which one of the following correctly matches the event with its date concerning the merger discussions?
1. Meeting of the Chief Ministers at Hyderabad House, New Delhi — 22 October 1955
2. Gentlemen’s Agreement — 20 February 1956
3. Warangal Congress meeting — 8 July 1954
accepted.x: All three date-event pairs are correctly matched: the Warangal meeting was on 8 July 1954, the Chief Ministers met at Hyderabad House on 22 October 1955, and the agreement was signed on 20 February 1956.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure date-event pair and verify the remaining chronological pairs.
accepted.sec: Hyderabad State - period, Burgula ministry, merger debate, 1954 shift

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents the linguistic composition of Hyderabad State as given in the demographic figures?
accepted.x: The population of Hyderabad State was 18.7 million, comprising Telugu speakers at 47.8%, Marathi speakers at 24.3%, Urdu speakers at 11.6% and Kannada speakers at 10.5%.
accepted.tq: Compare each percentage with its language rather than relying only on the largest group.
accepted.sec: Hyderabad State - period, Burgula ministry, merger debate, 1954 shift

accepted.s: The Telangana Regional Committee was constituted in 1958 under which constitutional provision?
accepted.x: The Telangana Regional Committee was constituted in 1958 under Article 371(1), with appointment by the President.
accepted.tq: Use the exact Article-number distinction among special constitutional provisions.
accepted.sec: Telangana Regional Committee and Mulki Rules

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Telangana Regional Committee:
1. It consisted of elected representatives from Telangana.
2. All Telangana ministers except the Chief Minister were ex officio members.
3. Disputes between the Committee and the State Government were to be referred to the Centre for final decision.
4. Its working was to be reviewed after ten years.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. The Committee represented Telangana legislators, included Telangana ministers other than the Chief Minister ex officio, referred disputes to the Centre and was subject to review after ten years.
accepted.tq: Check composition, dispute settlement and review clauses separately before selecting the complete combination.
accepted.sec: Telangana Regional Committee and Mulki Rules

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT among the subjects assigned to the Telangana Regional Committee?
accepted.x: The Committee dealt with regional matters such as planning, irrigation, agriculture, industry, recruitment, health, education and prohibition. Foreign affairs was not among its subjects.
accepted.tq: Find the subject outside the regional administrative and developmental sphere.
accepted.sec: Telangana Regional Committee and Mulki Rules

accepted.s: The Mulki Rules originated during which period and required approximately how much local residence for eligibility for local government employment?
accepted.x: The Mulki Rules originated in the Nizam’s era in 1919 and required about 15 years of residence for eligibility for local jobs. This differed from the 12-year domicile provision in the 1956 Agreement.
accepted.tq: Separate the Mulki residence requirement from the different domicile period in the Gentlemen’s Agreement.
accepted.sec: Telangana Regional Committee and Mulki Rules

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding the later history of the Telangana Regional Committee is correct?
o: It was extended for five years in 1968 and wound up after the 32nd Amendment in 1973.
It was extended for ten years in 1968 and abolished by the 42nd Amendment in 1976.
It was abolished in 1968 after the 32nd Amendment.
accepted.x: The Committee was extended for five years in 1968 and was subsequently wound up after the 32nd Amendment in 1973 removed Andhra Pradesh from Article 371(1).
accepted.tq: Link the extension, constitutional amendment and final consequence in sequence.
accepted.sec: Telangana Regional Committee and Mulki Rules

accepted.s: Under the power-sharing clause concerning the Deputy Chief Minister, if the Chief Minister belonged to Andhra, the Deputy Chief Minister was to belong to:
o: The majority linguistic group in the Assembly
accepted.x: The agreement provided that the Deputy Chief Minister should come from Telangana when the Chief Minister came from Andhra, and vice versa.
accepted.tq: Apply the reciprocal regional-balance rule to the stated hypothetical.
accepted.sec: Deputy Chief Minister post - clause and fate

accepted.s: Besides the Deputy Chief Minister’s post, the agreement provided that Telangana should receive one of which of the following portfolios?
o: Defence, External Affairs, Finance, or Railways
Finance, Revenue, Planning and Development, Commerce, or Industry
Education, Culture, Tourism, or Irrigation only
accepted.x: Telangana was to receive one of the portfolios of Finance, Revenue, Planning and Development, Commerce or Industry.
accepted.tq: Choose the option containing the exact set of regional power-sharing portfolios.
accepted.sec: Deputy Chief Minister post - clause and fate

accepted.s: Which of the following statements correctly describes the fate of the Deputy Chief Minister’s post under Sanjiva Reddy?
o: Sanjiva Reddy appointed a Telangana Deputy Chief Minister immediately.
Sanjiva Reddy did not appoint a Deputy Chief Minister and described the post as a “sixth finger”.
Sanjiva Reddy retained the post but transferred its powers to the Regional Committee.
The post was abolished by the 32nd Constitutional Amendment before the formation of Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.x: Sanjiva Reddy did not appoint a Deputy Chief Minister and dismissed the post as a “sixth finger”. This breach contributed to the grievances that led to the 1969 Jai Telangana movement.
accepted.tq: Use the exact action and quoted description to distinguish the event from later constitutional changes.
accepted.sec: Deputy Chief Minister post - clause and fate

accepted.s: The Pataskar Award was associated with which of the following matters?
o: Distribution of Hyderabad State’s linguistic population
Appointment of the Telangana Regional Committee
Allocation of Telangana seats in the Legislative Assembly
Settlement of the Andhra–Madras boundary dispute
accepted.x: The Pataskar Award was concerned with settling the Andhra–Madras border. Most of Tiruttani taluk of Chittoor went to Tamil Nadu.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a boundary award from committees dealing with state formation and regional safeguards.

accepted.s: The Nizam Andhra Mahasabha developed out of which organisation founded in 1921?
accepted.x: The Nizam Andhra Mahasabha grew out of the Andhra Jana Sangham, which was founded in 1921.
accepted.tq: Use the organisation-to-successor relationship rather than confusing it with later political bodies.
accepted.sec: Nizam Andhra Mahasabha - founding, first session

accepted.s: Which of the following best describes the historical role and later development of the Nizam Andhra Mahasabha?
o: It was a body created after 1956 to administer the Telangana Regional Committee.
It functioned only as a religious organisation and opposed all political activity.
It was formed exclusively to settle the Andhra–Madras boundary and remained administratively united.
It served Telugu cultural and political awakening in the Nizam’s State and later split into moderate and Communist groups.
accepted.x: The Nizam Andhra Mahasabha became a vehicle for Telugu cultural and political awakening in the Nizam’s State and later divided along moderate and Communist lines.
accepted.tq: Identify the option combining the organisation’s purpose with its later internal division.
accepted.sec: Nizam Andhra Mahasabha - founding, first session
